decisions.rationale: Reproduced on a fresh git archive of ea630d09 with the private completed work plus one added probe rule each, full suite in the pinned Chromium: a paused animation holding a reduced scale on both tags, a paused animation holding a different width on the day tag, a finite animation lasting about a day holding a reduced scale on both tags, and a short animation with a day-long delay and backwards fill holding a reduced scale on both tags each pass all 12 tests. The same unmodified pages, opened with no test handling and read at 0.3s, 3.3s and 6.5s, draw the tags at the wrong size every time. Line 142 finishes every animation whose end time is finite regardless of play state or how far away the end is, and finish() un-pauses and jumps past an effect the learner keeps seeing, so the task 11 Outcome ('exactly 200px wide on screen') and README line 17 ('It rejects scaling ... a tag or the checklist itself') are false for these pages. Medium is right, graded like the accepted cl4-sme-001: a wrong page passes, but only after a deliberate, implausible keyframes rule, and the calculated width is still required. The critic's recommendation to measure every non-settling animation as drawn is necessary but not sufficient: a 5s-delayed endless scale and a slow endless width animation are already measured as drawn at HEAD and still pass all 12, because nothing is drawn wrong at the instant measured. Smallest correct fix: finish only animations on the checklist, the tags and their ancestors that are running, finite and end within a few seconds, and fail task 11 on every other such animation unless all properties declared in its keyframes, read from the stylesheet source rather than getKeyframes(), are on a short paint-only allowlist, then add paused, long, long-delay and delayed-endless variants to the solved-run matrix and align README line 17 and the lab.json notes sentence.

Reproduced on ea630d09 with the private completed work: a 1s no-fill entrance animation that grows the .page wrapper from a reduced scale fails task 11 only, with 'lays out 200px wide but is drawn ... something around it is scaling it', while the same page opened with no test handling draws both tags correctly from 3.3s on. Lines 137 and 140 to 144 settle animations only on the checklist and the two tags, so an ancestor's short entrance is measured mid-flight, and the lab.json notes sentence does not say it covers only those elements. Low is right: the error is fail-safe, the edit is unusual and the message points at the right region. Smallest correct fix: extend the cl5-edu-001 settling rule from the checklist and tags to the checklist's ancestors, so this case is fixed by the same change with no extra code path.

Reproduced on ea630d09 with the private completed work: hiding the day tag with display none fails task 11 only, on the control assertion, and the cause text blames 'something around the tag (a wrapper, a float beside it, columns or positioning on the checklist)', because the ownReason chain at lines 177 to 186 has no branch for a display of none. The message therefore misdirects, against README Troubleshooting line 208 ('the message names the cause'). Low is right: the edit is implausible, the tag visibly vanishes and no wrong page passes. The README wording mismatch ('positioned absolute' versus 'positioned it absolutely') is real but cosmetic. Smallest correct fix: add a display-none branch to ownReason beside the contents branch, saying the tag is not drawn, and optionally reword the absolute and fixed cases to match README line 208.

Same root cause as cl5-edu-001, and reproduced the same way on ea630d09: the paused scale and paused width variants, a day-long finite scale, a 5s-delayed endless alternating scale on both tags and a 60s endless width animation on the day tag each pass all 12 tests, while the unmodified pages draw the tags wrong at 6.5s (the delayed one) or at every reading (the others). The loop-4 accepted fix, which finishes finite animations and measures endless ones as drawn at one instant, narrowed the class but cannot close it because it samples time. The critic's recommended mechanism, inspecting effect.getKeyframes() for size, box or transform properties, is also incomplete, and this is a reconciler-found route no critic reported: in the pinned Chromium getKeyframes() omits custom properties, returning no property for a keyframes rule that sets only a custom property and only opacity when one also sets opacity. A paused animation of a custom property that feeds the tags' scale, the same with a 5s delay and endless iterations, and the delayed one mixed with opacity each pass all 12 tests and draw both tags wrong, and a getKeyframes() denylist or allowlist classifies all three as harmless. In-page CSSOM cannot replace it, because reading cssRules from the file:// stylesheet throws a SecurityError, so the keyframe properties must be read on the Node side from the stylesheet source, as tasks 1 to 3 already do. I prototyped that classifier outside the repository over 23 variants: together with the existing measurements it fails every page that is drawn wrong once settled, and passes every page drawn correctly except two endless or delayed translate bobs, which README line 17 already rejects and one of which already fails at HEAD. Medium is right for the same reason as cl4-sme-001. Smallest correct fix: the single rule stated under cl5-edu-001, with custom properties treated as outside the allowlist, plus the variants listed there and custom-property paused and delayed variants in the solved-run matrix.

Reproduced on ea630d09 with the private completed work: a short fade-up entrance with both-way fill on the tags fails task 11 only with 'not by scaling, rotating, moving or zooming it', and a short scale-in entrance with both-way fill on the checklist fails task 11 only with 'The gear checklist itself is scaled, rotated, translated or zoomed', although both pages draw the tags correctly at every reading and the same entrances without fill pass all 12. After finish() the fill holds an identity value (the computed transform reads as an identity matrix, which DOMMatrixReadOnly reports as isIdentity), and lines 146 to 149 and 193 compare computed strings with 'none' and '1'. The same fade-up and checklist variants pass all 12 at a942501c with the loop-4 tests, so the tag case is a loop-5 regression and the checklist case is new with the loop-5 checklist check. Low is right: the page is valid and only the message misdirects, and nothing in the lab asks for an animation. This fix is also a precondition for the cl5-edu-001 rule, because that rule finishes short entrances and then measures their held end state. Smallest correct fix: treat geometric identity as unscaled for the tags and the checklist (identity transform matrix, zero translate, unit scale, zero rotate, zoom of one) and add both-way-filled entrance variants on the tags and the checklist to the valid rows of the solved-run matrix.
